author: jochembrouwer
content:
Here is a random idea. EIP spec is leading, we use AI to one-shot the implementation of this EIP on all clients, including EELS for spec+tests. Then we run these tests against all clients. If there are divergences (we can also one-shot with multiple models or run them multiple times) this means that the EIP spec is ambiguous or has uncovered certain edge cases (which AI then likely fills in with "own interpretation" (randomness)), which should then be fed back as feedback to EIP authors/champions.

The divergence "amount" (not entirely sure how to measure this) would give an indication of the work to do on the spec side.
**Note that even if all clients (unlikely) agree on the spec in a one-shot, this does not mean that the spec itself (the EIP) is correct, and should obviously be thorougly analysed to see that this is what we actually want, and does not introduce unwanted side effects (similar to what we are obviously doing now).** This would mean more eyes on the "high level specification" and less (?) "work" (in terms of human time/labour) on the code itself.

We can use this measure to create a rough plan for devnets (which EIPs to add on which devnet). Note that if we can one-shot two EIPs this could obviously mean that combining the two leads to new edge cases or divergences (this itself would be a nice experiment).

I might come back to this text later to correct some details. I think the most important thing is that we check the spec, because clients agreeing on the code does not mean that the spec (EIP) itself is correct 🙂
Would love to hear some thoughts.
